thread:
lina: Heads up — nightly SDLC pipeline failed on staging build. SAST/DAST job errored out when trying to decrypt the signing key from KMS. CI step: `kms-decrypt-artifact`. Anyone oncall? :eyes:
michael: I see the failure in the logs: 403 PermissionDenied on the cryptoKey path. Probably an RBAC change for the CI SA. infra-bot posted the raw snippet.
infra-bot: build log excerpt:
```
ERROR: KMSDecrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller does not have permission 
resource: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/artifact-signing
```
jess: did we rotate the key or the SA last night? I ran a quick check, no rotation PRs in infra repo. Could be a role removal during the cleanup. @kevin any recent IAM churn?
kevin: I deleted a couple of stale role bindings from the onboarding script earlier (cleanup of old SAs). I didn't touch `ci-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` but I may have removed a group that granted cloudkms access. Lemme check audit logs.
dara: we should capture the KMS audit event for Decrypt and the IAM policy change that led to it, attach to the ticket. Use Cloud Logging filter: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"' --limit=50` and for IAM changes: `protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy"`.
michael: confirmed — there's an IAM SetIamPolicy at 2025-09-03T03:02:11Z removing binding for group `ci-kms-access@redwood` (actor: kevin@redwood). That explains it.
jess: For short-term mitigation can we grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to the CI SA scoped to the specific cryptoKey? Prefer least privilege.
kevin: yes applying that now to `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/artifact-signing` — will post commit.
snyk-bot: SAST scan queued; note there are open low-confidence SQLi-like findings in `deploy/helm/values.yaml` that will re-run after CI is unblocked.
lina: thanks. Two asks: 1) capture audit evidence (IAM change + KMS decrypt failure) in the security ticket, 2) add a preventive check so future IAM cleanup runs don't remove the `ci-kms-access` group binding without an approved PR (maybe a pre-merge rule).
dara: for (1) I exported the log links and attached them to SEC-5123. For (2) we can add a pre-merge CI gate that verifies KMS access for the service account using a dry-run decrypt against a test key (no real key material). Example check: `gcloud kms keys testIamPermissions artifact-signing --keyring=ci-keys --location=global --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`. Put it in the infra repo as `ci/verify-kms-access.sh`.
michael: will open a small PR with the RBAC grant + the `verify-kms-access` gate. We'll scope the grant to the single key. Also adding an audit tag and linking to SEC-5123 for traceability.
lina: nice. Quick followups: can we also ensure the SAST/DAST runs surface a clearer failure message in the pipeline (currently it's a generic decrypt failure and hides which job failed)? That will help oncall faster.
kevin: agreed. I can add better logging in the decrypt wrapper to include job name and key path.
jess: reminder: add a test in the security review checklist to confirm KMS bindings for CI and Dedicated runners (two places). I'll add that to the next sec-review doc.
lina: closing the immediate incident: CI unblocked at 03:47Z after RBAC grant. Leaving SEC-5123 open to track followups: policy change (preventative gate), improved pipeline logging, and audit retention check. Thanks all :party_parrot:
